text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

The panel's composition doesn't help you here. Both you and the appointee are women, so sex can't plausibly explain why she was chosen over you — an all-female panel picking a woman over another woman is not a pattern that points anywhere. Raising it would likely read as grasping and undermine your credible complaint.

Your real argument is qualifications: you hold a master's in educational leadership and five years of actual leadership experience; she has "courses" and classroom experience only. That's a documentable gap, and the burden is on the employer to justify it.

Chase the written explanation in writing, citing your legal entitlement to reasons, with a deadline. Silence after two weeks is itself worth noting.
